description.narrative: Contribute to the improvement of the Human Rights situation in Southeast Asia through education and applied research.
Research network within democracy and human rights in colaboration with the ASEAN University Network.

Stöd till ett forskningsnätverk inom mänskliga rättigheter i ASEAN-regionen. Det svenska stödet avser en forskningsfond, nätverkande/konferenser/workshops, utveckling av kursplaner för lokala utbildningar, doktorandutbildning och MSc-utbildning, samt utbyte av seniora forskare.
Budgeten bedöms som rimlig i jämförelse med andra liknande forskningsnätverk.

The achieved results of SHAPE-SEA phase 1 are assessed to be very satisfactory. SHAPE-SEA made important contributions to research capacity in Southeast Asia, in particular in the field of human rights research. SHAPE-SEA grants, seminars, exchanges and publications have expanded the space for generating new knowledge about the state of human rights and peace in Southeast Asia. This was achieved, despite the fact that academic freedoms are continuously threatened in the region.
SHAPE-SEA itself, a programme under Mahidol University with leadership from two regional academic networks, was a new initiative. SHAPE-SEA is assessed to have been successful in operating due in large part to the strong commitment and dedication of its leadership and staff at the Secretariat at Mahidol University, and the scholarly community of human rights and peace researchers in Southeast Asia.
The capacity for applied research and education that was built during phase 1 of SHAPE-SEA can be sustained through the continued work of scholars and educators that were trained, and whose research was funded, during phase 1. Meanwhile, the sustainability of the SHAPE-SEA programme is still largely dependent upon Sida financial support. Sida remains one of the few sources for regional research support in the field of human rights and peace studies.
Phase 1 of the SHAPE-SEA program has contributed to the building of a region-wide network of human rights and peace scholars that produces new knowledge and contributes to discussions and debates on human rights and peace in Southeast Asia. During Phase 1 more than 200 scholars received training on human rights and peace research design and methods, and 58 research projects were completed. Twelve books were published by SHAPE-SEA with more than ten thousand downloads from their website. Seventeen policy briefs hae been produced and seven high-level policy outreaches have been carried out with ASEAN and Southeast Asian governments to promote human rights and peace education.
Also during Phase 1, a SHAPE-SEA Secretariat was established at Mahidol University that has successfully managed SHAPE-SEA activities.
The 2020 external evaluation found that the SHAPE-SEA programme has produced a range of relevant outputs that have been highly appreciated by participants and consistently of high quality. It finds that the programme has contributed to improve the standard of research and education in the area of human rights and, to a lesser extent, peace. It has also contributed to an increased body of human rights and peace research about Southeast Asia produced from within the region, and it has had important consequences for academic freedom. Examples of achievements from the first phase of SHAPE-SEA (2015-2019) include 58 research grants, three commissioned research projects, five editions of the Human Rights Outlook in Southeast Asia, and 2 international scholarly conferences on human rights and peace. Likewise, partly due to SHAPE-SEA outreach to ASEAN and its Member States, ASEAN adopted a proposal to include Human Rights and Peace Education in universities, and included the aim in the five year working plan of the ASEAN Intergovernmental Commission on Human Rights (2021-2025).
A Human Rights Based Approach and Gender Equality review commissioned by the Embassy during 2020 found that HRBA and GE were mainstreamed in all of SHAPE-SEA Phase 1 projects and activities.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
